**M5 and M10, judged by this seat (not the author's label).** Both differ from the code only on an input no test, register
case or pipeline path makes: a SECOND op writing rows of the SAME role / entity / ordinal key. Probe `zzprobe-samekey.test.ts`
(the mirror, under the code and under each mutant, the source restored and compared equal): kerb `base:0` at L2
(3142, 2862) – (499, 2966), then a second chain with the same key `base:0` at L2 from (2430, 2874) to (2400, 1500) —
it lands at (2431, 2890) on the first op's edge (`atFold: true`, degree 3). Code: `isSplit: true` (the pair is not
this op's); M5: `isSplit: false`. Everything else is equal: `allProblems` and `dissolvableProblems` empty, a third
chain `x:1` attached there and removed leaves the vertex (`vStays: true`, degree 3 either way), and `base:0`'s removal
takes both chains and the vertex (`vertexCount: 4`, the frame). M10: `base:0` at L1 along y = 2000 crossed twice by a
`base:0` L2 chain — code: both crossings `split: [true, true]`; M10: `[true, false]` in one direction (the second
crossing on the pair this op made, whose rows are the key at L1); degree 4 both, no problem, no dissolvable vertex, and
the key's removal takes everything. So on honest inputs (one key per op — every test, the register and, by reading,
every pipeline caller) both are equivalent, and on the same-key input the difference is one flag bit with no observable
effect on any removal this seat could construct (the vertex has degree ≥ 3 while the key lives; the key's removal
frees it). PLAUSIBLE equivalent on reachable inputs; CONFIRMED different on the contrived one. Not a wrong result on an
honest input, not a shortcut, not a gate: a hardening test (note N-22), under J162 / J169 and the blocker rule.

## Probes (the mirror)

* **P3 — C-0302 (3)'s open case (the coincident-chain split vertex), judged here as the brief asks.**
  `zzprobe-coincident.test.ts` (saved as `probe-coincident.test.ts.saved`; its output `probe-coincident.json`):
  `base:A` L2 (3142, 2862) – (499, 2966); `base:C` L2 (3142, 2862) (499, 2966) (2430, 2874) — shares A whole
  (`W_STRETCH_SHARED` ×2 at (3142, 2862)) and folds back onto the shared edge, its third point attracted to
  (2431, 2890) (`W_ATTRACTED` ×1 at (2430, 2874)); the vertex v there is C's own shape vertex (`placed[2]`) AND a split
  of A's run, so by C-0302 (3)'s rule it keeps the flag (`vSplit: true`, degree 2, neighbours (3142, 2862) and
  (499, 2966); `dissolvableProblems` empty because the rows are two keys). Then `x:1` L2 (0, 3501) (735, 705)
  (2456, 2886) attaches at v (`xPlaced2IsV: true`, degree 3) and is removed in a later batch: v is dissolved
  (`vLiveAfterXRemoved: false`, 7 → 6 vertices; the print, chunk refs and level digests differ from before x by that
  vertex only — the edge (499, 2966) – (3142, 2862) carries `base:A` and `base:C` as before). `allProblems` is empty
  at every step; `base:C`'s removal then restores A exactly (`restoresA: true`); the control without x restores A too;
  deterministic across runs. **Judgement: a notes row, not a blocker.** Every committed result is a valid arena
  (no throw, no invalid output, deterministic — N-45's fail-safe bars hold); the geometry after x's removal equals the
  geometry before it (v lay on A's edge within the hot pixel, between C's own collinear rows); what differs is a
  canonical-form question — whether C's fold-back vertex survives a later chain's lifecycle — of the same shape as N-13,
  in a class (a chain sharing another's whole edge and folding back onto the shared stretch) that no register kind,
  N-47 case or pipeline path reaches. The alternative, clearing the flag, would leave the vertex as residue on A's edge
  when C goes (Q9's shape), so the flag cannot carry both meanings: that is design the seats may not add (J156), and
  C-0302 (3) reports it to the session as such. Note N-23.
* **`foldedBase` 0** — the Q10 row above (`zzfolded0.test.ts`, a copy of M0-a-06's `restore.test.ts` with its three
  `foldedBase` assertions set to `toBe(0)`; PR size; 22 passed).
